title: Competitor behavior probe cases and signal harvester
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Background: As open-model availability and vendor feature sets accelerate, we need a lightweight, repeatable way to collect structured competitor behavior signals (latency profiles, quantization variants, API contract deviations, pricing micro-deltas) across regions and workload archetypes. Existing model-landscape docs are high-level; this ticket produces a reproducible 'signal harvester' toolkit and a prioritized set of probe cases that PM, Eng, and Solutions can run with minimal setup.

Goal: Deliver a small, instrumented playbook + artifact set that captures normalized signals across 6 competitor endpoints and 4 synthetic workload archetypes. Output is a CSV/BigQuery-ready schema and a short ops runbook so field teams can re-run probes monthly or on-demand after vendor changes.

Scope (what we'll deliver):
- Probe case catalog (24 cases): regional latency, 1-shot vs streaming, embeddings throughput, quantization-downsampled accuracy, tokenization edge-cases, structured-output stability.
- A lightweight harvester script (Python, `harvester.py`) that runs each probe, collects latency histograms, token counts, error types, and response similarity scores.
- Standardized schema & README for storage (example BigQuery table schema + mapping).
- Rapid runbook for Solutions/SEs and a one-page exec summary for GTM.
- Short dashboard spec (Console view) for top-line signals (latency P50/P95, error rate, compat drift) to feed into weekly model-watch sync.

Out of scope: Deep model-quality evaluations (e.g., adversarial NLG scoring) and long-running synthetic workloads. We will hand off to Research for deeper experiments.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Harvester runs end-to-end in < 45m for the full 24-case matrix under a CI job and uploads results to the canonical storage path.
2) Probe outputs conform to the supplied schema and include required tags (region, model-id, quantization-flag, run-timestamp).
3) Two field tests run by Solutions with different accounts (one NA, one EU) and documented results.
4) Short Console dashboard mock attached and product review approved.

Metrics for success:
- Reproducibility: 95% of probe runs succeed without manual fixes.
- Signal density: At least 8 actionalizable signals per vendor (latency, error spike, API diff, tokenization mismatch).
- Time-to-run: Full matrix completes within target window in >= 90% of CI runs.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1 (PM + Eng): finalize probe matrix, schema, and runbook draft.
- Week 2: Eng builds harvester, basic telemetry, and upload path.
- Week 3: Run field tests (NA/EU), iterate on flaky cases.
- Week 4: Product review, dashboard mock, and publish runbook to Confluence.

Links & artifacts:
- Draft probe matrix (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MKT/pages/Competitor+Harvester+Draft
- Harvester repo (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/market-harvester/pull/12
- Example payloads and schema: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/market-harvester/samples

Stakeholders:
- PM: Priya Desai (owner)
- Eng: Liam O'Connor (lead), Ana Cortez (runtime advisor)
- Solutions/SE: Carlos Mendes (field runs)
- Research: Elena Fischer (quality handoff)

Risks & trade-offs:
- Running probes against commercial endpoints runs the risk of rate-limiting; we will throttle test concurrency and add retry backoff.
- Vendor TOS may restrict certain automated probes; Solutions will validate account-level permissions before running.
- Harvester aims for speed over depth; for deep model regressions we'll flag and pass to Research.

Next steps: finalize matrix with Eng by 2026-02-02, land initial harvester PR by 2026-02-16, and schedule Solutions field runs for week 2026-02-23.
